body.en: Topic 5 develops differential and integral calculus: limits, derivatives from first principles, product/quotient/chain rules, tangent and normal lines, optimization, definite integrals, areas between curves, and rectilinear kinematics.

label.en: ● Level 1 Foundation — The Derivative from First Principles

body.en:
The derivative represents the instantaneous rate of change of a function, defined as the limit of average rates of change across an infinitesimal interval \(h\):

\[ f'(x) = \frac{dy}{dx} = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x + h) - f(x)}{h}. \]

Geometrically, the difference quotient \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}\) is the gradient of the secant line connecting \((x, f(x))\) and \((x+h, f(x+h))\). As \(h \to 0\), the secant line approaches the tangent line at \((x, f(x))\).

Standard Elementary Derivatives:

\[ \frac{d}{dx}(x^n) = n x^{n-1}, \quad \frac{d}{dx}(e^{kx}) = k e^{kx}, \quad \frac{d}{dx}(\ln x) = \frac{1}{x} \quad (x > 0), \]\[ \frac{d}{dx}(\sin x) = \cos x, \quad \frac{d}{dx}(\cos x) = -\sin x, \quad \frac{d}{dx}(\tan x) = \sec^2 x = \frac{1}{\cos^2 x}. \]

Local Linearization & Differentiability: A function \(f\) is differentiable at \(x = a\) if and only if the difference quotient \(\lim_{h \to 0} \dfrac{f(a+h) - f(a)}{h}\) exists as a finite real number. Differentiability at \(x = a\) strictly implies continuity at \(x = a\), but the converse fails at sharp corners (e.g. \(|x - 2|\)), vertical tangents, or jump discontinuities.

label.en: ● Level 2 Analytical Tools — Differentiation Rules & Optimization

body.en:
Operational Calculus Rules:

  • Product Rule: \[ (uv)' = u'v + uv'. \]
  • Quotient Rule: \[ \left(\frac{u}{v}\right)' = \frac{u'v - uv'}{v^2}. \]
  • Chain Rule: For composite \(y = f(g(x))\): \[ \frac{dy}{dx} = f'(g(x)) \cdot g'(x) \iff \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy}{du}\cdot\frac{du}{dx}. \]

Tangents, Normals & Optimization:

  • Tangent Line: At \((a, f(a))\), \(y - f(a) = f'(a)(x - a)\).
  • Normal Line: At \((a, f(a))\), \(y - f(a) = -\frac{1}{f'(a)}(x - a)\) (provided \(f'(a) \neq 0\)).
  • Stationary Points: Critical points satisfy \(f'(x) = 0\).
  • Second Derivative Test: Let \(f'(c) = 0\):
    • If \(f''(c) < 0\): \(f\) is concave down \(\implies\) local maximum at \(x = c\).
    • If \(f''(c) > 0\): \(f\) is concave up \(\implies\) local minimum at \(x = c\).
    • If \(f''(c) = 0\): test inconclusive; evaluate sign change of \(f'(x)\).
  • Point of Inflection: A point where the curve changes concavity, requiring \(f''(x) = 0\) with a sign change in \(f''(x)\).

label.en: ● Level 3 University Rigor — Integration, Area Between Curves & Kinematics

body.en:
Indefinite Integrals & Reverse Chain Rule:

\[ \int x^n\,dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C \;(n \neq -1), \quad \int \frac{1}{x}\,dx = \ln|x| + C, \quad \int e^{kx}\,dx = \frac{1}{k}e^{kx} + C, \]\[ \int \sin(kx)\,dx = -\frac{1}{k}\cos(kx) + C, \quad \int \cos(kx)\,dx = \frac{1}{k}\sin(kx) + C. \]

Integration by substitution / reverse chain rule:

\[ \int f'(g(x))g'(x)\,dx = f(g(x)) + C, \quad \int \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\,dx = \ln|f(x)| + C. \]

Fundamental Theorem of Calculus & Area:

\[ \int_a^b f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a) \quad \text{where } F'(x) = f(x). \]

The exact geometric area between curves \(y = f(x)\) and \(y = g(x)\) from \(x = a\) to \(x = b\) is:

\[ A = \int_a^b |f(x) - g(x)|\,dx = \int_a^b (y_{\text{top}} - y_{\text{bottom}})\,dx. \]

Rectilinear Kinematics: For a particle moving along a straight line with position \(s(t)\):

  • Velocity: \(v(t) = s'(t) = \frac{ds}{dt}\).
  • Acceleration: \(a(t) = v'(t) = s''(t) = \frac{dv}{dt}\).
  • Displacement across \([t_1, t_2]\): \[ \Delta s = s(t_2) - s(t_1) = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} v(t)\,dt. \]
  • Total Distance Travelled across \([t_1, t_2]\): \[ \text{Total Distance} = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} |v(t)|\,dt. \]

Why Differentiability Implies Continuity & How Implicit Differentiation Works: Notice that for \(x \ne a\), we can write \(f(x) - f(a) = \dfrac{f(x) - f(a)}{x - a}\cdot (x - a)\). Taking the limit as \(x \to a\) by the Product Law gives:

\[ \lim_{x \to a} \bigl(f(x) - f(a)\bigr) = f'(a)\cdot 0 = 0 \implies \lim_{x \to a} f(x) = f(a) \]

Similarly, when differentiating an implicit relation \(F(x, y) = c\) with respect to \(x\), \(y = y(x)\) is an inner function of \(x\). By the Chain Rule, \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\bigl[y^n\bigr] = ny^{n-1}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\), and for product terms \(\dfrac{d}{dx}[xy] = y + x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).

label.en: Worked Example 5.1 — Derivative from First Principles

problem.en: Use the limit definition of the derivative from first principles to find \(f'(x)\) for \(f(x) = 2x^2 - 5x + 3\).

solution.en:
1. State the first principles limit definition:
\[ f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x + h) - f(x)}{h}. \]

2. Expand \(f(x + h)\):
\[ f(x + h) = 2(x + h)^2 - 5(x + h) + 3 = 2(x^2 + 2xh + h^2) - 5x - 5h + 3 = 2x^2 + 4xh + 2h^2 - 5x - 5h + 3. \]

3. Compute the difference \(f(x + h) - f(x)\):
\[ [2x^2 + 4xh + 2h^2 - 5x - 5h + 3] - [2x^2 - 5x + 3] = 4xh + 2h^2 - 5h = h(4x + 2h - 5). \]

4. Divide by \(h\) (for \(h \neq 0\)) and evaluate the limit:
\[ f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{h(4x + 2h - 5)}{h} = \lim_{h \to 0} (4x + 2h - 5) = 4x + 0 - 5 = 4x - 5. \]

Result: \(f'(x) = 4x - 5\). ∎

label.en: Worked Example 5.2 — Optimization & Second Derivative Test

problem.en:
An open-topped rectangular cardboard box is to be constructed with a square base of side length \(x\text{ cm}\) and height \(h\text{ cm}\). The total surface area of cardboard available is \(300\text{ cm}^2\).
(a) Express \(h\) in terms of \(x\).
(b) Show that the volume is given by \(V(x) = 75x - \frac{1}{4}x^3\).
(c) Find the dimensions \(x\) and \(h\) that maximize the volume, proving that this yields a global maximum.

solution.en:
(a) Surface area consists of 1 base plus 4 vertical sides:
\[ A = x^2 + 4xh = 300 \implies 4xh = 300 - x^2 \implies h = \frac{300 - x^2}{4x} = \frac{75}{x} - \frac{x}{4}. \]

(b) Volume: \[ V(x) = x^2 h = x^2\left(\frac{300 - x^2}{4x}\right) = \frac{x(300 - x^2)}{4} = 75x - \frac{1}{4}x^3. \]

(c) Differentiate: \[ V'(x) = 75 - \frac{3}{4}x^2. \]
Set \(V'(x) = 0\):
\[ 75 - \frac{3}{4}x^2 = 0 \implies \frac{3}{4}x^2 = 75 \implies x^2 = 100 \implies x = 10\text{ cm} \quad (x > 0). \]
Test for maximum using second derivative:
\[ V''(x) = -\frac{6}{4}x = -1.5x. \]
At \(x = 10\): \(V''(10) = -15 < 0\), which confirms a local maximum.
Since the physical domain is \(0 < x < \sqrt{300}\) and \(V(0) = 0, V(\sqrt{300}) = 0\), this critical point is the unique global maximum.
Height: \[ h = \frac{300 - 10^2}{4(10)} = \frac{200}{40} = 5\text{ cm}. \]
Maximum volume: \(V = 10^2 \times 5 = 500\text{ cm}^3\).

label.en: Worked Example 5.3 — Area Between Intersecting Curves

problem.en: Find the exact area of the finite region enclosed by the parabola \(y = 4 - x^2\) and the line \(y = 2 - x\).

solution.en:
1. Find points of intersection:
\[ 4 - x^2 = 2 - x \implies x^2 - x - 2 = 0 \implies (x - 2)(x + 1) = 0 \implies x = -1 \quad \text{and} \quad x = 2. \]

2. Determine top and bottom curves on \([-1, 2]\):
At \(x = 0\): \(y_{\text{parabola}} = 4\) and \(y_{\text{line}} = 2\). Hence, \(y_{\text{top}} = 4 - x^2\) and \(y_{\text{bottom}} = 2 - x\).

3. Set up the definite integral:
\[ A = \int_{-1}^2 [(4 - x^2) - (2 - x)]\,dx = \int_{-1}^2 (2 + x - x^2)\,dx. \]

4. Integrate analytically:
\[ \left[ 2x + \frac{x^2}{2} - \frac{x^3}{3} \right]_{-1}^2 = \left( 4 + 2 - \frac{8}{3} \right) - \left( -2 + \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} \right) \] \[ = \left( 6 - \frac{8}{3} \right) - \left( -\frac{7}{6} \right) = \frac{10}{3} + \frac{7}{6} = \frac{20}{6} + \frac{7}{6} = \frac{27}{6} = \frac{9}{2} = 4.5. \]

The exact enclosed area is 4.5 units².

label.en: ⚠ Topic 5 Exam Traps: Distance vs Displacement & Derivative Rules

body.en:
Displacement vs Total Distance: Displacement is the net integral \(\int_{t_1}^{t_2} v(t)\,dt\); total distance travelled is \(\int_{t_1}^{t_2} |v(t)|\,dt\). If velocity changes sign, you must split the integral at every root where \(v(t) = 0\).

Quotient Rule Minus Sign Order: The numerator is \(u'v - uv'\), NOT \(uv' - u'v\). Subtracting in the reverse order produces an incorrect negative derivative.

Inflection Point Justification: \(f''(x) = 0\) is a necessary condition for a point of inflection, but NOT sufficient. You must explicitly show that \(f''(x)\) changes sign across that point (e.g. \(f(x) = x^4\) has \(f''(0) = 0\), but \(x=0\) is a minimum, not an inflection point).

Problem (Medium): Find \( f'(x) \) given \( f(x)=-5x^{2}-5x-5 \).

Step-by-Step Solution: Working through this calculus step: Differentiate term by term using the power rule: \( f'(x)=-10x-5 \). [M1] [A1]

caption.en: Error Diagnosis — Common Student Traps vs. Exam-Board Method (Calculus)

rows.en: Inflection points like \(f(x) = x^3\) at \(x = 0\) have \(f'(0) = 0\) without changing sign.
Verify that \(f'(x)\) actually changes sign across \(x = c\) (or check \(f''(c) \ne 0\)).
Differentiate \(dy/dx\) with respect to \(t\), then divide by \(dx/dt\).
Forgetting product rule on \(xy\) in implicit differentiation
Treats \(y\) as a constant instead of \(y(x)\).

body.en: Exam Justification Rule (IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis & Approaches / Applications & Interpretation SL): When justifying local extrema or points of inflection on free-response questions, state "because \(f'(x)\) changes sign from positive to negative at \(x = c\)" rather than referring vaguely to "it" or "the graph."

Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \(y' = 3x^2 - 6x - 9 = 3(x^2 - 2x - 3) = 3(x - 3)(x + 1)\).

question.en:
Practice 5.2: A particle moves in a straight line with velocity \(v(t) = 3t^2 - 12t + 9\text{ m/s}\) for \(0 \le t \le 4\).
(a) Find the times at which the particle is momentarily at rest.
(b) Calculate the net displacement of the particle over \([0, 4]\).
(c) Calculate the total distance travelled by the particle over \([0, 4]\).

solution.en:
(a) \(v(t) = 0 \implies 3(t^2 - 4t + 3) = 0 \implies 3(t - 1)(t - 3) = 0 \implies t = 1\text{ s}\) and \(t = 3\text{ s}\).

(b) Displacement: \[ \Delta s = \int_0^4 (3t^2 - 12t + 9)\,dt = \left[ t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t \right]_0^4 = (64 - 96 + 36) - 0 = 4\text{ m}. \]
(c) Total distance requires splitting the integral where velocity changes sign:
Over \([0, 1]\): \(v(t) > 0\); \(\int_0^1 (3t^2 - 12t + 9)\,dt = [t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t]_0^1 = 4\text{ m}\).
Over \([1, 3]\): \(v(t) < 0\); \(\int_1^3 (3t^2 - 12t + 9)\,dt = [t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t]_1^3 = (27 - 54 + 27) - 4 = 0 - 4 = -4\text{ m}\), so distance is \(|-4| = 4\text{ m}\).
Over \([3, 4]\): \(v(t) > 0\); \(\int_3^4 (3t^2 - 12t + 9)\,dt = [t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t]_3^4 = 4 - 0 = 4\text{ m}\).
Total distance travelled = \(4 + 4 + 4 = 12\text{ m}\).
